title: Strategic actions and value iteration on the Perfection-tuned base bot
question: Does a policy from finite-horizon value iteration over the full integer state, choosing one of five strategic actions per turn, score reliably higher than the Perfection-tuned bot it steers, and higher than the best single action played every turn?
change: Experiment 15 unchanged except the setup: learner base bot greedy-full-probe-perf, 4 players, opponents greedy-full-probe-perf, greedy-full-combo-perf and the anchor greedy-full-probe-perf (rl-gate defaults on dev da04376).
method: Value iteration on 300k random-action games; min-count chosen on 2,000 validation games; final paired test on 10,000 evaluation seeds
setups: Perfection, 16×16 continents, 4 players, Crazy, seat 0 Xin-Xi (human seat), learner base greedy-full-probe-perf; opponents greedy-full-probe-perf, greedy-full-combo-perf, greedy-full-probe-perf (anchor), seats shuffled per seed (rl-gate defaults)
